reuseEvidence.licenseInfo: Les géodonnées sont mises à disposition sous forme d’Open Government Data (OGD). Elles peuvent être utilisées, partagées et réutilisées gratuitement. Lors de l’utilisation, il faut en indiquer la source : « Source : Etat de Fribourg » ou « © Etat de Fribourg ».
reuseEvidence.geocatAccessNote: XML requests on 2026-09-08 returned HTTP 403/500 or a login page; no geometry vintage established from that linked record.
reuseEvidence.assessment: Explicit dataset OGD terms permit attributed vector sharing/reuse. The catalogue title incorrectly says stops, but its URL and serviceItemId identify the service containing polyline layer 1. All 128 original line geometries and all original attributes match exactly; OGD adds TYPE_LIGNE. Reuse is resolved independently of the ordinance product mapping. Geometry vintage and physical direction remain unverified; retain an archival study release.

timetable.publisher: SBB / Open data platform mobility Switzerland
timetable.refreshPolicy: Pinned September 2026 research fixtures; not a live or current-service feed. A new timetable or geometry release requires a complete rebuild and admission audit.

roads.dayModel: civil day with preceding service-day spillover
roads.scope: Every full Fribourg-calling bus pattern on both civil dates, including night and replacement buses; exact agency, route, platform IDs and coordinates retained.

source.description: Geofabrik Switzerland 2026-09-02 plus OSM border extract retrieved 2026-09-08

roads.model: Inferred bus road paths; complete-pattern consensus fallback only; not operator-verified

policy.admission: Fill failed official pairs only when every full bus pattern containing that route-specific directed platform pair has a valid identical road path. Explicit matcher failures and conflicting pattern contexts remain excluded. Provisional geographic membership and demand-responsive services remain excluded.
policy.directionNote: Inferred paths using bus/PSV access and direction tags. The pinned pfaedle profile uses penalties, not an absolute one-way prohibition; legal direction and temporary restrictions are not certified.

rail.validityNote: Catalogue dates and verified bytes do not establish September 2026 alignment validity. Inferred infrastructure paths, not certified service running tracks.
rail.transformation: Existing XTF parser; LV95 simplification 5 m and swisstopo approximate LV95-to-WGS84 transformation rounded to 6 decimals.
rail.reuseNote: Reused the hashed national FOT snapshot already acquired for Thurgau. No fresh acquisition or current-alignment claim. Explicit TPF gauge and dated works evidence accompany this Fribourg application.

supportingDocuments.purpose: TPF standard-gauge Fribourg–Ins and Broc–Romont corridors; gauge evidence, not geometry vintage.
Sunday 6 September 2026 from 21:00: no S50/S51 trains Bulle–Semsales. Also identifies 2025–2027 metric-line rebuilding; no new FOT admission of that altered corridor.

policy.admission: Fill failed cantonal rail pairs using exact operating-point numbers and standard-gauge infrastructure. All full directed pattern contexts must agree; block other called stations out of order. Keep all original calls and existing accepted paths. No nearest-station, operator-name or platform override. Meter-gauge, gauge-changing and unreviewed TPF special routes remain outside this supplement.

census.boundaryRule: At least one original GTFS call coordinate in the unsimplified 2026 Fribourg canton polygon. Full journey retained, including every call outside Fribourg. No operator whitelist.
census.allYearMeaning: All trip records in the pinned annual archive, including records inactive on both validation dates; not a claim of operating every day.

boundarySensitivity.note: Metre-level WGS84/LV95 approximation; platforms within 10 m of the boundary are flagged on both sides. Routes supported only by those platforms are provisional geographic members. No polygon buffer applied.

weekdaySundayPatterns.key: GTFS route identity + direction_id + full ordered original platform IDs, including repeats and out-of-canton calls

timing.note: Original GTFS times retained, including minute-rounded equal timestamps. Zero-duration segments are not speed observations and no artificial travel time is invented.

repairs.evidence: The two disconnected components of the same official TPF line 9 feature end 11.22 mm apart near Charmettes. Collapse only this pinned endpoint onto the other original endpoint; keep both source snapshots unchanged. This is an inferred precision repair, not surveyed topology or road-direction evidence.

scopeLimits: GTFS fixed-stop archive and all cantonal line records inventoried; services absent from both sources and GTFS-Flex service areas are not a verified census of every real-world service.
Two September civil days do not establish holiday, winter or year-round pattern coverage.
Cross-boundary journeys keep all calls. Entire patterns still failing any segment after the audited road and rail fallback are excluded; a source extent alone never truncates a trip.
Geometry combines cantonal line, inferred OSM road and inferred FOT rail paths; not observed movement, legal one-way validation, running-track selection or temporary diversion confirmation.
